solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Arousing crazed fan, be shameless

indicators.note: arousing stirs things up, so the following letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these three words, punctuation ignored

explanation.surface: Someone whipping up an excitable supporter is urged to show no shame about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be' looks like part of the definition, but its letters belong to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A brazen-faced person shows no embarrassment, so the compound adjective is a synonym for unabashed or impudent.

clue.text: Fuel alternative beside oil

indicators.note: an alternative version of the following words is a different arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: An alternative energy source sitting next to conventional oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' reads as describing the fuel, a fair hint at its green credentials, but it signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Biodiesel is a kind of motor fuel made from plant or animal fats, so it is an example of fuel.

clue.text: Pleasantness of chaps absorbed by basic toys regularly seen

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter at a steady interval
what is absorbed by something ends up inside it

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Simple toys giving children pleasure, with some grown men joining in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters across both words as one run, ignoring the space between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenity can mean the quality of being agreeable or pleasant, an older literal sense of the word.

clue.text: Conflict between journalist and princess briefly in earlier era

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective placing something in a past period

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter of the name is dropped
something between two others sits inside them, splitting them apart

blocks.note: ED, an editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A clash between a newspaperman and a royal, recalled from times gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: The princess is Diana, Princess of Wales; 'Conflict' sits between the two people, as the clue says.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwardian describes the reign of Edward VII, 1901 to 1910, a period well in Britain's past.

clue.text: Nicer penalty, striker’s last

indicators.note: last asks for only the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A football commentator thinks a late spot kick by the striker was a nicer touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Finer and nicer are both comparatives meaning of better quality or more pleasing.

clue.text: He acted badly and broke rules

indicators.note: done badly, the words are mangled and their letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A man misbehaved and flouted the regulations.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheat is to act dishonestly against the rules, so the past tense matches having broken them.

clue.text: Discussed Scandinavian’s stoop

indicators.note: something discussed is spoken about, so the sound of the word counts, not its spelling

blocks.note: a Dane is a person from Denmark

explanation.surface: Talk about a Nordic person's bad posture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stoop' looks like a hunched back, but here it is the verb meaning to lower oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to condescend to do something beneath one's dignity, the figurative sense of stooping.

clue.text: Starter of cheese, honey and spice

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: honey is a term of endearment, like love

explanation.surface: A menu: a cheese course, then honey, then something spiced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'honey' reads as food on a menu, but it is the affectionate name for a loved one.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloves are dried flower buds used whole or ground, a common kitchen spice.

clue.text: Plan steps of tedious task on ordinary diagram

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: Someone plans the stages of a boring job using a standard chart.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the task above the rest. 'steps' sounds like stages of work; they are dance steps.
explanation.definitionFit: To choreograph is to arrange the moves of a dance, deciding the sequence of a performer's movements.

clue.text: Pale dune vacated by group that’s nomadic

indicators.note: a vacated word has been emptied, leaving just its outside letters

blocks.note: a ring is a group, as of conspirators

explanation.surface: A sandy desert left behind by a band of travelling people.
explanation.definitionFit: Wandering peoples move from place to place without a fixed home, which is what nomadic describes.

clue.text: Advances sure to follow Scottish inventor’s flops

indicators.note: to follow tells us the word before it is placed after the next piece

blocks.note: Alexander Graham Bell, the Scottish-born inventor of the telephone; the possessive is a link

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's inventions keep failing despite all the progress made.
explanation.definitionFit: To go belly up is an idiom for failing completely, as a business collapses or a dead fish floats.

clue.text: Noted player Oscar I introduced to organ

indicators.note: something introduced to another thing is put inside it

blocks.note: Oscar is O in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A famous musician talks about the Oscar and introducing a church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' and 'organ' suggest music, but the player is an actor. Laurence Olivier was a celebrated English stage and screen actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivier was a famous actor, and player is an old word for actor, so he is an example of a noted player.

clue.text: Personnel from Universal welcomed by entire cast

indicators.note: someone welcomed by others is taken in among them
cast can mean thrown about, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: U is the film classification for universal

explanation.surface: A film studio's staff greeted warmly by the whole cast of actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Universal' and 'cast' suggest a Hollywood studio; U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the group of attendants or staff accompanying an important person, so it denotes personnel.

clue.text: Somewhat critically assess reflective written composition

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the following words is used
a reflection shows things the other way round, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of critically and the start of assess

explanation.surface: A rather harsh assessment of a thoughtful piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflective' looks like it describes the composition, but it signals reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is a short piece of prose writing on a subject, as set in schools, so it is a written composition.

clue.text: Imprisoned Juliet and old boy for crime involving corrupt worker

blocks.note: inside is slang for being in prison
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A woman and a former pupil were jailed for a crime involving a bent employee.
explanation.definitionFit: An inside job is a theft or crime carried out with help from someone employed by the victim.

clue.text: Fraught son flusters around

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into another order

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A worried boy gets his family in a fluster.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraught situation causes anxiety and tension, which is what stressful means.

clue.text: Sailor apt to consume endless rum and vegan fare

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter
to consume something is to take it inside

blocks.note: a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor
apt and fit both mean suitable

explanation.surface: A sailor is inclined to drink rum while eating plant-based food.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack, from jack tar, is old slang for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Jackfruit is a large tropical fruit whose texture makes it a popular meat substitute in vegan cooking.

clue.text: Underground worker good with aged subordinate, we’re told

indicators.note: we are told means we hear it spoken, so only the sound matters

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A reliable member of a resistance movement teams up with an elderly junior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underground' hints at secret resistance work; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold miner digs for gold, often in deep mines below the surface, so is an underground worker.

clue.text: Maiden in Germany with determined attitude

blocks.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A young woman living in Germany with a resolute outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'determined attitude' reads as one phrase, but determined belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A mindset is a person's established way of thinking or outlook, close in meaning to attitude.

clue.text: Boozer on the doorstep‘s drunk alcohol away from house

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady and muddled, so the letters stagger into a new order
away from says the following letters are taken out

blocks.note: HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A drunkard at someone's door has been drinking away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' suggests a heavy drinker; in British slang it is also a pub, and your local is the pub nearest home.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is the neighbourhood pub a person regularly visits, the boozer close by.

clue.text: Outsiders from Nanjing invested in new Seoul airport areas

indicators.note: the outsiders of a word are its first and last letters
a new version of the word has its letters arranged afresh
money invested in something is put into it

explanation.surface: Chinese money is being put into a new Korean airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Airports have lounges, waiting rooms where passengers sit before boarding, so these are airport areas.

clue.text: Man sold nuts and seeds

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

explanation.surface: A trader sold nuts and seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts and seeds' reads as a product line, and the answer is in fact a nut; 'nuts' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically the edible part of an almond is the seed of its fruit's stone, so almonds are seeds.

clue.text: Beastly sound from rotating object that’s painful

indicators.note: rotating turns the word round so it reads the other way

blocks.note: an aim is an object or goal
ow is the cry of pain

explanation.surface: A horrible noise comes from a spinning thing that hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' reads as nasty; it means made by a beast, here a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Miaow is the cry a cat makes, an animal noise, so it is the sound of a beast.

clue.text: One in flight originally accommodated within jail

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the next word
within places that letter inside the other word

explanation.surface: An airline passenger was first held in a prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests a plane; it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a series of steps between floors, so a single stair is one member of it.

clue.text: Section of Elvis quiff you oiled

indicators.note: a section is a part, so the letters lie within the following words

blocks.note: the letters running from the end of Elvis into the start of you

explanation.surface: Part of a rock star's greased-up hairdo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oiled' looks like hair grease; it is British slang for drunk, as is squiffy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for slightly drunk or tipsy.

clue.text: Cloth garment with mark on front beginning to fade

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the head is the front, as of a queue
a lasting mark on the skin

explanation.surface: A fabric item with a stain on the front that is starting to fade.
explanation.definitionFit: A headscarf is a square of fabric worn over the head, an item of clothing made from cloth.

clue.text: One crabby lead in Rambo collected by film runner

indicators.note: the lead in a word is its first letter
collected by means taken in and held inside

blocks.note: Forrest Gump, the film character famous for running

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered action hero teamed up with a famous movie runner.
explanation.definitionFit: A grump is a bad-tempered, irritable person, and crabby means irritable.

clue.text: Engineer James goes round turning on nearby facilities

indicators.note: turning sends the next word round the other way
going round something means surrounding it

blocks.note: James Watt, the Scottish steam engineer

explanation.surface: An engineer travels round converting local amenities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facilities' is the polite euphemism for toilets.
explanation.definitionFit: A water closet is a flushing toilet, and facilities is a common euphemism for toilets.
